expectations.text: The response identifies g_wstats (the per-worker `struct worker_stats` array, the four ~13-15% lines) as false sharing: each worker writes its own element, but the 16-byte elements of 8 workers sit on the same 128-byte line at different offsets.
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] response.md:7 '#1-#4 (...d200-...d380) | g_wstats[0..31]: rx_packets at 0x0, 0x10, ... rx_bytes at 0x8, 0x18 ... Each offset is touched by only 1-2 CPUs | 54.5% | False sharing'; :14 'Each worker writes only its own slot, but struct worker_stats is 16 bytes, so 4 workers share every 64-byte line'; :19 'up to 3 neighbouring workers, or 7 counting the adjacent-line pair' (8 per 128-byte pair).

expectations.text: The response identifies `g_state.inflight` (offset 0x0 of the 33.8% line, written by all 32 workers) as true sharing, and says padding or alignment alone won't fix it.
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] response.md:8 '#0 (...d100), offset 0x0 | g_state.inflight: atomic_fetch_add/atomic_fetch_sub ... from 32 CPUs | True sharing (a contended atomic)'; :15 'Padding does nothing for this; the only fix is to stop sharing the counter'; :3 'padding can't fix that'.

expectations.text: The response notices that the read-mostly `shutting_down` flag (offset 0x10, read in every worker's loop condition) shares that cache line with the constantly written `inflight` counter, and recommends moving it to a separate cache line.
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] response.md:9 '#0, offset 0x10 | g_state.shutting_down, read on every loop iteration (:51), on the same line as inflight | False sharing'; :29 'g_state is split. shutting_down and log_level (both read-mostly) share one 128-byte block'; diff at :43 puts _Alignas(128) on shutting_down; :82 'Moving shutting_down off the counter's line doubles it again'. Implemented in files/stats.h:33-39.

expectations.text: The response recommends giving each worker's stats their own cache line (e.g. `alignas(64)` or padding `struct worker_stats` to 64 bytes or more, or per-thread allocation), with code.
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] response.md:27 'struct worker_stats is now _Alignas(128). Each worker owns a whole 128-byte block'; the diff at :31-38 shows the code; files/stats.h:21-27 has _Alignas(PKTSRV_DESTRUCTIVE_SIZE) plus a _Static_assert on the alignment.

expectations.text: The response recommends taking the shared atomic `inflight` counter off the per-packet path (e.g. per-worker counters that the monitor sums, batching, or dropping it), rather than only padding it.
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] response.md:28 'The global inflight is gone. It is now a per-worker 0/1 field in the same block, and the monitor adds them up'; the diff at :48-60 and files/pktsrv.c replace atomic_fetch_add/sub with relaxed stores to ws->inflight, which the monitor sums.

expectations.text: The response treats the remaining lines (each 3.1% of HITMs or less, e.g. the ring buffers and malloc's main_arena) as minor and doesn't recommend changes for them.
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] response.md:87 'Still left: the rings (~10%; not changed because ring.c wasn't attached)', followed by three recommended ring changes: 'Cache the other side's index', 'Pop and push in bursts', 'Move the two indices 128 bytes apart'. It treats the rings as a ~10% item it would have fixed, not as minor lines to leave alone. Only malloc is deprioritized ('not worth chasing until the rest is fixed').

expectations.text: The response suggests re-running perf c2c and/or the thread-scaling benchmark after the change to confirm that the HITMs on these lines drop.
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] response.md:100-103 'Re-run c2c. Rebuild, then repeat the same perf c2c record -g ... Lines #0-#4 should disappear' and 'Run --threads 1/2/4/8/16/32 before and after and compare the monitor's pkts/s'.

eval_feedback.overall: 06 doesn't say whether an optional, deferred suggestion counts as recommending changes. A passed because its only ring idea is explicitly optional ('If you want to trim this later') and sits under a 'not the cause of your scaling problem' heading. B failed because it has a dedicated 'Still left' section with imperative ring changes and says they were 'not changed because ring.c wasn't attached'. Consider stating where that line is.
